record.original_question: For a regular polynomial automorphism f of C^d, construct a compact complex manifold S̄(f) containing the quotient S(f)=Ω(f)/⟨f⟩ as the complement of a divisor, prove uniqueness of S̄(f) up to bimeromorphism, and describe its complex geometry and deformation space.

evidence.quote: Problem 9. — Let f ∈ Aut[Cd] be any regular polynomial automorphism. 1. Prove that one can find a compact complex manifold S¯(f) ... 2. Prove that S¯(f) is unique up to bimeromorphism. 3. Describe complex objects on S¯(f) ... Compute its deformation space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f \in \mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{C}^d)$ be a regular polynomial automorphism, in the sense that $f$ extends as a birational map to $\mathbb{P}^d$ and the indeterminacy sets $I^+$ of $f$ and $I^-$ of $f^{-1}$ on the hyperplane at infinity are disjoint. Let $K^\pm = \{z \in \mathbb{C}^d : (f^{\pm n}(z))_{n\ge 0} \text{ is bounded}\}$, let $J^\pm = \partial K^\pm$, and define the escaping (or "current support / non-wandering at infinity") set
$$\Omega(f) = \mathbb{C}^d \setminus (K^+ \cup K^-),$$
on which $f$ acts properly discontinuously and freely. Let $S(f) = \Omega(f)/\langle f \rangle$ be the quotient complex manifold.

Carry out the following three tasks.

1. Construct a compact complex manifold $\bar S(f)$ together with an open embedding $S(f) \hookrightarrow \bar S(f)$ such that the complement $\bar S(f) \setminus S(f)$ is a (closed analytic) divisor.

2. Prove that such a compactification $\bar S(f)$ is unique up to bimeromorphic equivalence: any two compact complex manifolds $\bar S_1(f)$, $\bar S_2(f)$ as in (1) are bimeromorphic via a map extending the identity on $S(f)$.

3. Describe the complex geometry of $\bar S(f)$ (its Kodaira dimension, the structure of natural complex objects such as holomorphic forms, line bundles, and currents on it) and compute its deformation space (e.g., the Kuranishi space of $\bar S(f)$ and the dimension of $H^1(\bar S(f), T_{\bar S(f)})$).
artifact.status_search_result: This is listed as Problem 9 in a recent list of open problems on Hénon-type (regular polynomial) automorphisms. No published construction of such a compactification with proof of uniqueness and computation of the deformation space appears to be available; the problem is regarded as open.
